attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the claim in his own words.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the structural claim without asserting impossibility of mitigation. The named models illustrate the argument. Explaining hallucinations through how LLMs work is causal.

contract.note: Structural propensity is a fair ordinary reading. The contract appropriately excludes universal inevitability and the separate recommendation to pursue different approaches.

evidence.note: Establishes statistical hallucination mechanisms under explicit calibration and fact-distribution assumptions. Supports structural propensity, while expressly allowing mitigation.
The broad computability result does not isolate the practical causes of factual hallucinations in ordinary LLM use.
Abstention reduces hallucinations in tested models and tasks. This limits an inevitability interpretation but does not contradict a structural propensity.
Published before the cutoff, this later research clarifies statistical and incentive mechanisms and possible remedies. It is not a measurement of the April 2024 models.

reviews.rationale: Under the contract's fair structural-propensity reading, e1 establishes a statistical source of hallucinations beyond isolated implementation defects. Its assumptions limit the conclusion; mitigation evidence does not negate that mechanism. The packet does not establish universal inevitability or a need to replace LLMs.
